stories.title: Banyan Street, Independencia Refi South Florida Office With $54M
stories.excerpt: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management have nabbed $53.5 million to refinance an office complex in Doral, Fla. Wells Fargo provided the financing that backs the 290,000-square-foot Doral Center property. The 10.8-acre campus includes two buildings — one rising six stories and the other seven — at 3750 Northwest 87th Avenue and 8750 Northwest 36th Street in the Miami suburb. Doral Center, built between 1985 and 1990, is about 85 percent leased, according to CBRE, whose Amy Julian and Andrew Chilgren brokered the debt. Tenants include coworking operator Quest Workspaces, which leases about 38,000 square feet. The owners have spent $15.5 million updating the asset since buying it for $43 million in 2020 during the height of the pandemic. The 2020 sale price was about $4.3 million less than what the property had traded for four years earlier, according to property records. “The extensive capital improvements have completely transformed Doral Center into a premier workplace environment,” Julian said in a statement. “This strategic repositioning, combined with South Florida’s robust economic fundamentals, has enhanced the property’s competitiveness and triggered an immediate surge in leasing activity.” This January, the joint venture sold about three acres for $6 million to residential developer ROVR Development. A representative for Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Banyan Street and Independencia refi Doral office complex for $53.5M via Wells Fargo
290K SF, 85% leased Doral Center; owners invested $15.5M capex since 2020 pandemic purchase
South Florida office repositioning signals stabilization, but multifamily demand impact minimal
stories.summary: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management secured $53.5 million in refinancing from Wells Fargo for Doral Center, a 290,000-square-foot office complex in Miami's Doral suburb. The property, built 1985–1990 and currently 85% leased, has received $15.5 million in capital improvements since acquisition in 2020. The refi suggests stabilization in South Florida office, though values remain depressed versus pre-pandemic levels.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Office refi activity doesn't signal demand drivers (jobs, in-migration) for apartments; instead reflects distressed asset recovery. Monitor if office-to-residential conversions accelerate in Doral as office recovery stalls.

stories.title: Indian Restaurant Samudhra Takes 10K SF at 312 West 43rd Street
stories.excerpt: New Jersey-based Indian restaurant Samudhra is establishing a presence across the Hudson River in Hell’s Kitchen. The eatery signed a 10,000-square-foot lease on the ground level of the Ellery at 312 West 43rd Street, owned by Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors, for its second location in the U.S. following its first restaurant in Franklin Park, N.J., according to the landlords. Taconic did not disclose the asking rent or the length of the lease, but asking rent for prime retail space in the nearby Times Square retail corridor of Broadway and Seventh Avenue from 42nd to 47th streets was $1,400 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Samudhra brings a premium new dining and social experience that will serve both our residents and the broader neighborhood,” George Tsapelas, senior vice president of Taconic, said in a statement. “From the outset, our vision for the Ellery has been to create a dynamic mixed-use destination that contributes to the energy of the area, and Samudhra further strengthens the retail and dining mix we’ve curated at the property.” CBRE’s Lon Rubackin, Michael Kadosh and Bevan Cohen negotiated on behalf of the landlord while Brad Schwarz from Lee & Associates handled the deal for the tenant. CBRE and Lee & Associates did not immediately respond to requests for comment. “The Ellery provides an exceptional setting for our New York City location and gives us the opportunity to introduce our distinctive premium Indian dining and lounge experience to a much broader audience,” Mangesh Chinthamaneni, founder and CEO at Samudhra, said in a statement. The announcement comes almost exactly a year after German grocery chain Aldi signed a lease spanning 25,000 square feet on the ground floor of the building in late August 2025 as part of Aldi’s broader rollout across the U.S. The New York Post first reported Samudhra’s lease deal. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Samudhra Indian restaurant leases 10K SF ground retail at 312 W. 43rd St., Hell's Kitchen
Prime Times Square corridor rents $1,400/SF in Q2 2026; mixed-use tenant commitment signals recovery
Retail demand on Hell's Kitchen/mixed-use sites growing, but minimal bearing on residential rents
stories.summary: Samudhra, a New Jersey-based Indian restaurant, signed a 10,000-square-foot ground-level lease at The Ellery (312 West 43rd Street) in Hell's Kitchen for its second U.S. location. Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors own the mixed-use building. Prime retail in nearby Times Square commanded $1,400 per square foot in Q2 2026, reflecting retail market recovery.
stories.impact: Minor signal of neighborhood stabilization and foot traffic in Hell's Kitchen, which may boost multifamily desirability at nearby assets, but the retail lease itself does not move the needle on apartment demand or supply in Manhattan.

stories.title: East Harlem Housing Proposal on City-Owned Lot Expands to 762 Units
stories.excerpt: An affordable and supportive housing complex slated for a city-owned site in Manhattan’s East Harlem neighborhood just got 62 units larger. The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) submitted plans on Friday to rezone the city block surrounding 22 East 119th Street. The requested amendments will facilitate a housing project spanning three buildings with a total of 762 units. PincusCo first reported on the filing. The site is currently occupied by a six-story, 174-unit single room occupancy building where Volunteers of America–Greater New York hosts supportive housing for formerly homeless, single adults, many of whom are veterans. In accordance with a city policy that avoids “spot zoning” individual tax lots, the rezoning proposal would impact the entire East Harlem block, bounded by East 118th and East 119th streets, between Madison and Fifth avenues. In addition to the site’s designation as an urban renewal area and the disposition of city-owned property, HPD’s requested amendments would label the block as a Mandatory Inclusionary Housing area, ensuring affordable housing will be a part of any future redevelopments of the block’s privately owned buildings. A prior iteration of the project, sponsored by nonprofit Volunteers of America–Greater New York, planned 700 units across two buildings. Those included a 23-story supportive housing tower and a 25-story affordable housing tower. Plans also incorporated community space and commercial facilities for the nonprofit, with funding sought through HPD and the New York City Housing Development Corporation. Land use documents accompanying the newest proposal at 22 East 119th Street are not currently available. The change in site plans, and how surrounding buildings or project timelines will be impacted, is unclear. bullets: NYC HPD rezoning East Harlem block (E. 118–119th, Madison–5th Ave) for 762-unit affordable/supportive housing
Three-building project expands from 700 to 762 units; replaces 174-unit SRO with formerly homeless residents
City-led zoning and affordable pipeline constrains market-rate multifamily development on premium Manhattan sites
stories.summary: The NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development filed plans to rezone an East Harlem block at 22 East 119th Street to facilitate a 762-unit mixed affordable/supportive housing complex across three buildings. The site currently houses a 174-unit SRO operated by Volunteers of America serving formerly homeless individuals. The rezoning applies to the entire block between East 118th–119th streets and Madison–Fifth avenues to avoid spot zoning.
stories.impact: City zoning strategy prioritizes affordable and supportive housing on desirable Manhattan sites, reducing available land for market-rate multifamily development. East Harlem's affordability mandate and SRO preservation signal gentrification resistance; watch for spillover demand into adjacent submarkets (Upper East Side, Yorkville) where market-rate development may face less regulatory friction.

stories.title: Green Point Building 754K-SF Georgetown Spec Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Green Point Property plans to build a 754,000-square-foot spec building in Georgetown that could eventually have 3 million square feet of industrial space. It’s in the GTX Logistics Park at 1000 FM 972 The building costs are estimated at $42 million for the concrete tilt-wall warehouse shell that is scheduled to begin construction in October and be completed in November 2027. The Austin Business Journal reports the GTX Logistics Park is marketing 2.6 million square feet left on the 180 acres it still owns. Colliers International Group Inc.’s Travis Hicks and Chase Clancy handle leasing at the site. Georgetown is about 30 miles north of Austin with a population of nearly 107,000 people. Gree Point says its focus is on high-growth markets throughout Texas and the Southeastern US to acquire and develop industrial properties. Green Point’s team has 40 years of combined real estate investment experience and collectively has acquired, developed and managed real estate assets exceeding $3 billion across the United States. The post Green Point Building 754K-SF Georgetown Spec Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Green Point Property building 754K SF spec warehouse in Georgetown (30 mi. north Austin), est. $42M cost
GTX Logistics Park has 2.6M SF remaining on 180 acres; construction begins Oct., completes Nov. 2027
Industrial spec development in high-growth Texas market signals confidence, but not directly tied to multifamily
stories.summary: Green Point Property plans to construct a 754,000-square-foot spec warehouse at GTX Logistics Park in Georgetown, Texas (30 miles north of Austin, pop. ~107,000). The concrete tilt-wall shell carries an estimated $42 million cost, with construction slated for October 2026 to November 2027. The park holds 2.6 million square feet of remaining developable land across 180 acres.
stories.impact: Industrial construction in Georgetown signals developer confidence in high-growth Texas corridor, but Austin-area multifamily demand is more directly tied to corporate HQ relocations and tech employment. Monitor whether logistics job creation in Georgetown drives satellite multifamily demand in that submarket or reinforces sprawl away from core Austin.

stories.title: Truist Lends $277M on Jersey City Multifamily Tower Build
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Rockpoint and Urby has secured $277 million of construction financing to develop the second phase of a multifamily tower in Jersey City, Commercial Observer has learned. Truist provided the loan for the sponsorship’s 748-unit 201 Hudson – by Urby project along the Jersey City waterfront. Rockpoint and Ubry joined forces to acquire land at 201 Hudson Street for the project in July, CO first reported at the time. “This financing reflects Truist’s continued commitment to supporting premier sponsors pursuing transformative multifamily developments in high-growth urban markets,” said Rebecca M. Cox, senior vice president and market manager at Truist National Real Estate. The transaction was led by Katie Kennedy, Northeast market leader at Truist, with Walt Reece, a director of real estate syndicated finance at Truist Securities, leading the syndication, according to the firm. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Jordan Roeschlaub, Chris Kramer, Holden Witkoff and Jack Fenton. The brokerage firm also advised the joint venture partners on the joint venture capitalization with a team composed of Adam Spies, Adam Doneger and Michael Collins. Located in Jersey City’s Paulus Hook neighborhood, 201 Hudson – by Urby marks the second phase of a 69-story tower that will include 528,000 rentable square feet and 10,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Community amenities will include a pool, a fitness center and coworking spaces. Rockpoint, Urby and Newmark did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Truist provides $277M construction financing for Rockpoint/Urby's 748-unit Jersey City waterfront tower
201 Hudson Street project; Rockpoint and Urby acquired land July; active waterfront multifamily expansion
Northeast multifamily financing strong; Jersey City remains premier urban rental market with capital availability
stories.summary: Rockpoint and Urby secured $277 million in construction financing from Truist for the second phase of 201 Hudson—by Urby, a 748-unit multifamily tower along the Jersey City waterfront. The joint venture acquired the land in July. Newmark brokered the debt; Truist syndicated the loan, citing continued commitment to premier multifamily sponsors in high-growth urban markets.
stories.impact: Strong capital flow into Jersey City waterfront multifamily signals sustained investor confidence in the Hudson River submarket. This validates the waterfront as a competitive rental destination and likely tightens available development sites; developers should prioritize remaining assemblies in Jersey City's waterfront corridor before valuations exceed underwriting assumptions.

stories.title: Houston Office Building Owners Ink $250M Refi
stories.excerpt: PRP Real Assets and Riyad Capital secured a $250 million CMBS loan to refinance 777 Hidden Ridge, a 1.1 million-square-foot office property in Irving, Texas. Commercial Search reports that Bank of America originated the two-year, interest-only note with three one-year extension options. Previous debt includes a $253.8 million note issued by Citizens Financial Group in 2019, set to mature in 2029. KDC and Verizon completed the building in 2019, developed on a build-to-suit basis for Pioneer Natural Resources USA Inc. That same year, PRP and Riyad acquired the asset. Pioneer had inked a 20-year, triple-net lease set to run until 2039. The agreement has no early termination and no contractual rights for the remainder of the term. Pioneer has since left the building, but must fulfill the lease obligations. Pioneer is looking to sublease the space. The 10-story building has amenities such as a conference center, gym, coffee shop, on-site childcare, medical clinic and six-story parking garage with 2,569 spaces. The post Houston Office Building Owners Ink $250M Refi appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PRP Real Assets and Riyad Capital refi Irving office tower 777 Hidden Ridge for $250M CMBS via BofA
1.1M SF built 2019 for Pioneer Natural Resources; Pioneer departed, sublease hunt underway, 20-yr NNN lease continues
Office tenant exodus and forced sublease marketing in Irving signals distress; multifamily spillover unlikely near weak office
stories.summary: PRP Real Assets and Riyad Capital obtained a $250 million CMBS loan from Bank of America to refinance 777 Hidden Ridge, a 1.1 million-square-foot office building in Irving, Texas. Built in 2019 on a build-to-suit basis for Pioneer Natural Resources, the property is now vacant and marketed for sublease, though Pioneer remains obligated under its 20-year triple-net lease through 2039.
stories.impact: Pioneer's departure and forced sublease reflects broader Texas office distress; however, Irving is a secondary office market and unlikely to anchor multifamily demand. Conversely, if sublease fails, office-to-residential conversion could emerge as strategy; monitor Irving's regulatory stance on adaptive reuse.

stories.title: VIC Partners Obtains Construction Loan for 268-Unit FW Workforce Rental Community
stories.excerpt: VIC Partners obtained a $36.5 million primary line of credit for the construction of Vic Centre, a 268-unit workforce-housing development at 7120 Anderson Blvd. in Fort Worth outside of Loop 820 and north of Interstate 30. The project is being developed by Vic Partners and M-13 Construction. OakNorth Bank will provide the loan as part of a $48 million joint financing with Hickory CRE Capital, a commercial real estate lender. Concord Summit Capital arranged the construction loan. VIC suggests the cost of the construction will be $41.7 million. The development will consist of nine three-story residential buildings, a clubhouse, fitness center, pickleball court and business center along with 402 parking spaces.  The post VIC Partners Obtains Construction Loan for 268-Unit FW Workforce Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: VIC Partners obtains $36.5M primary line from OakNorth and Hickory CRE for 268-unit Fort Worth workforce housing
Vic Centre north of I-30, outside Loop 820; $41.7M total construction cost; 9 buildings, completion 2027–2028
Fort Worth workforce multifamily capital active; submarket demand supports mid-to-lower-cost product, not class-A competition
stories.summary: VIC Partners secured $36.5 million in primary construction financing (part of $48 million joint credit from OakNorth and Hickory CRE) for Vic Centre, a 268-unit workforce-housing development at 7120 Anderson Boulevard in Fort Worth. Total construction cost is $41.7 million. The nine-building complex will include amenities and is being developed by M-13 Construction.
stories.impact: Workforce housing construction in Fort Worth's emerging submarkets (north of I-30) signals tightening of affordable inventory and sustained demand for sub-market-rate product. Developers targeting workforce housing in DFW should prioritize land acquisition in similar outer Loop areas before valuations escalate, and expect strong leasing demand at 2028 stabilization.

stories.title: W Properties Mixing BTR and Garden-Style Apartments in Melissa
stories.excerpt: W Properties plans to build a 252-unit garden-style multifamily community on approximately 12 acres adjacent to Everbloom (shown), the company’s 343-unit build-to-rent community in Melissa, Texas. The company said it’s taking a different approach with garden-style apartments, a sector still working through elevated supply and concessions across North Texas. Texas multifamily permitting across its five major metros has fallen by more than half from its 2023 peak, while Dallas-Fort Worth continues to absorb a significant pipeline of apartments already under construction. W Properties Andrew Welker added, “BTR and garden-style apartments are different products, and we would not have started a garden-style project in that same environment. We expect to go vertical by mid-2027, positioning this community for an early 2029 leasing season, when we believe today’s supply pressure will look materially different.” The post W Properties Mixing BTR and Garden-Style Apartments in Melissa appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: W Properties building 252-unit garden-style community on 12 acres in Melissa, TX adjacent to 343-unit BTR
DFW multifamily permitting fell 50%+ from 2023 peak; W Properties delays to 2029 lease-up to clear supply
Developer timing strategy reveals market saturation anxiety; garden-style segment weaker than BTR, expects 2-year clearance window
stories.summary: W Properties plans a 252-unit garden-style multifamily community on 12 acres in Melissa, Texas, adjacent to its 343-unit build-to-rent property (Everbloom). The developer explicitly cited elevated supply and concessions across North Texas as reason to pursue garden-style (lower-tier) product. DFW permitting dropped over 50% from 2023 peak, and W Properties targets 2029 leasing to let market absorption clear current inventory.
stories.impact: Critical market signal: DFW oversupply is real and developer-acknowledged; permitting collapse confirms supply correction underway. W Properties' decision to lag a garden-style lease-up to 2029 implies current concessions are unsustainable. Developers exiting or delaying standard garden-style should reassess DFW fundamentals; strong sponsors may opportunistically acquire stressed 2024–2026 deliveries at discounts before 2029 recovery.

stories.title: REITs Post Record High FFO in Q2 2026: Nareit
stories.excerpt: REITs posted record highs for funds from operations (FFO) and net operating income (NOI) in 2026’s second quarter while maintaining strong balance sheets, according to Nareit’s latest REIT Industry Tracker. More than 70% of REITs reported year-over-year increases in FFO, while nearly 80% reported year-over-year increases in NOI. Industry Tracker data show that FFO reached $22.4 billion in Q2, up 12.4% Y-O-Y. Meanwhile, NOI reached $32.7 billion, up 6.8%. Additionally, same-store NOI experienced a 4.1% Y-O-Y gain, demonstrating that REIT operations outpaced inflation in the second quarter, which was 3.5% “The strength we’re seeing from the REIT industry isn’t coming from one measure or sector,” said John Worth, EVP of research & investor outreach at Nareit. “Across the board, REITs continue to generate strong income from their properties reflecting rising occupancy while maintaining robust balance sheets. That combination speaks to the underlying resilience of the industry amid ongoing economic uncertainty.” The post REITs Post Record High FFO in Q2 2026: Nareit appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Q2 2026 REITs report record FFO ($22.4B, +12.4% YoY) and NOI ($32.7B, +6.8% YoY); 70%+ FFO growth
Same-store NOI +4.1% YoY outpaces 3.5% inflation; strong balance sheets and rising occupancy driving performance
REIT fundamentals robust across sectors; capital markets remain well-bid, financing available for quality multifamily sponsors
stories.summary: REITs posted record highs for funds from operations and net operating income in Q2 2026, with FFO reaching $22.4 billion (+12.4% YoY) and NOI hitting $32.7 billion (+6.8% YoY). Over 70% of REITs reported year-over-year FFO growth, and nearly 80% reported NOI gains. Same-store NOI grew 4.1% YoY, outpacing 3.5% inflation; REITs maintained strong balance sheets.
stories.impact: REIT strength signals robust capital availability and investor appetite for multifamily across strong and stabilizing markets. Developers with quality projects and experienced sponsors should capitalize on favorable financing window before potential rate volatility. Watch for REIT acquisition signals in secondary markets where cap rates have widened; opportunistic sellers and distressed sponsors may face REIT interest.

stories.title: Mamdani Sets Sights on Fixing — Not Replacing — Deteriorating Section of BQE
stories.excerpt: Will Mayor Zohran Mamdani be the first administration to finally fix the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) along Brooklyn Heights? Mamdani announced Monday morning that the New York City Department of Transportation (DOT) would build bypasses around the surrounding neighborhoods and maintain access to local attractions while finally rebuilding the swiftly deteriorating cantilever portion of the freeway. DOT would build a two-level bypass above Furman Street from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights, sitting below the promenade and not extending above the current highway. The city would also create a second elevated bypass from Columbia Heights to the Manhattan Bridge. The Mamdani administration plans to start the estimated $4 billion project in 2030, despite a sense of urgency from officials. The city estimates the project could take 10 years. The Mamdani administration said it believes this renovation, as opposed to a replacement, will extend the life of the BQE for another 40 years. “After decades of kicking the can down the road and indecision that failed to yield substantial results, we will act with urgency to rehabilitate the city’s portion of the BQE to ensure the safety of New Yorkers and minimize the likelihood of massive traffic diversions into Brooklyn neighborhoods,” DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn said in a statement. “While the city and the state must right the wrongs of Robert Moses with the BQE and other infrastructure plowed through urban communities, decades of political paralysis have left us out of options.” For every year that the city procrastinates, costs increase by an estimated $160 million, according to the announcement. “For decades, prior administrations have failed to deliver urgent long-term repairs to BQE Central — but we can no longer afford to wait for the perfect solution,” Mamdani said in a statement. “We’re going to fix the aging concrete, repair the deteriorating triple cantilever and build temporary roads that keep the highway operabl
bullets: NYC Mayor Mamdani announces $4B BQE repair (not replacement) in Brooklyn Heights; project start 2030, 10-year timeline
Two-level bypass below Furman St. promenade; second elevated bypass to Manhattan Bridge; 40-year BQE lifespan extension target
Brooklyn Heights infrastructure renewal may accelerate residential development near BQE, but delays until 2030 remove immediate supply urgency
stories.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a $4 billion plan to repair (rather than replace) the deteriorating Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) along Brooklyn Heights. The project involves building two-level and elevated bypasses around Furman Street and toward the Manhattan Bridge, expected to extend the BQE's life another 40 years. Construction is planned to begin in 2030 with a 10-year timeline.
stories.impact: BQE stabilization reduces uncertainty for nearby Brooklyn Heights multifamily development but provides no near-term demand catalyst (project start 2030). Developers with land in Brooklyn Heights should factor in extended construction period (2030–2040); conversely, post-2030 BQE confidence may support lease-up velocity for buildings stabilizing during repair phase. Monitor for air rights or TOD zoning near bypass segments.
